summary: A brick light on a 100-foot Chesapeake bluff at Elk Neck, lit 1833: women keepers, a 1921 rescue, and a volunteer group that reopened the tower in 2024.

lens.where: stolen after automation (nomination); a 250 mm solar-powered acrylic optic replaced it during automation and was removed when the light was decommissioned in 2000 (nomination)

structures.note: Raised a story in 1889; demolished about 1971 (nomination) or 1972 (LighthouseFriends).
Fog bell room erected April 1888 over a dry well; demolished about 1971 (nomination).

access.note: Area open daily 8 a.m. to sunset; interior opened by a volunteer group; tower climbs on volunteer-staffed weekend hours, weather permitting; parking limited; inside Elk Neck State Park.

facts.agency: Maryland Department of Natural Resources (owner); Turkey Point Light Station, Inc. (volunteer group that manages the light)

events.note: US Lighthouse Society gives 1832 as the year the station was established.
Commenced operation in 1833 (LighthouseFriends); tower built 1833 (nomination).
Tower and keeper's quarters built by John Donahoo for $4,355.
Fresnel lens installed; the nomination later calls it fourth-order.
Lanterns replaced; funded April 1866, work completed 1867.
Fog bell room prefabricated at the Lazaretto depot and erected in April 1888.
Keeper Caleb B. Stowe towed a disabled power boat with seven men to Town Point Wharf.
Keeper C. W. Salter towed a disabled barge that was being towed by a disabled motor boat; May 1923.
Fannie May Salter appointed keeper with the personal authorization of President Coolidge after Civil Service objections.
Unspecified repairs after hurricane damage (nomination).
Station electrified in 1942 (nomination); the nomination's other passage gives 1943.
Changed from fixed white to flashing white 'when the station was automated' (nomination).
Automated after Fannie Salter's retirement (nomination); roster ends her service 1948.
Keeper's quarters and outbuildings demolished about 1971 (nomination); LighthouseFriends gives 1972.
Decommissioned April 2000.
Leased to Turkey Point Light Station, Inc., a non-profit.
Reactivated as a private aid to navigation on 30 November 2002.
Property transferred to the State of Maryland, which leased the light to the volunteer group.
Replica fog bell tower completed; an 1891 bell mounted in June 2023.
Closed March 2024 for trail and parking work; reopened September 2024.

notes_for_editor: 1. First lit: the nomination dates the tower to 1833; LighthouseFriends says the light commenced operation in 1833; the USLHS record gives 1832 as the year the station was established. The story uses 1833 and states 1832. 2. Focal height: the nomination gives 129 feet above the water (39.3 m, used in facts); the USLHS record gives 65 feet above the water (19.8 m) and a 30-foot height to the lantern centre. Not reconciled; the story gives the nomination figure and says the sources differ. 3. Range: the nomination says 'visible for 13 miles' with no unit; not converted. 4. Characteristic: the record's 'Fl W 6s' appears in none of the sources read, so it is not in facts. The nomination says fixed white, changed to flashing white in 1947. Check the Coast Guard Light List. 5. Electrification: 1942 (nomination, p. 9) against 1943 (nomination, p. 11). 6. Automation: 1947 flashing change against 1948 automation (nomination); the roster and LighthouseFriends give Fannie Salter's retirement as August 1947 (LighthouseFriends says 1947) and the roster ends her service 1948. 7. Quarters demolition: about 1971 (nomination) or 1972 (LighthouseFriends). 8. Georgiana S. Brumfield: 54 years living at the station (nomination) against 64 years (Prince George's Enquirer, 28 Nov 1919, OCR read directly). Start 26 July 1895 (nomination) against 25 July 1895 (Midland Journal, 10 Oct 1919, OCR). 9. The Cecil Whig death notice of 2 March 1912, p. 7: OCR reads 'Mrs. Ell abeth Lusby' and 'maay years'; the name and 'maay' were not checked against the page image. The notice names her as keeper when she died in 1912, which conflicts with the roster's 1862 end date for her service; its remark 'We believe he was appointed by General Jackson' does not fit her 1844 appointment. Left unreconciled and stated in the story. 10. The Midland Journal (10 Oct 1919) says Mrs. Crouch was appointed 'after the death of Mrs. Lusby'; the roster has Cloman from 1862 and John Crouch from 1865. Stated in the story; the Prince George's Enquirer's remark that her father 'took charge' in a year printed '18CI' in the OCR is unreadable and not used. 11. OCR-matched entries: the Commissioner of Lighthouses FY1921 entry for Caleb B. Stowe was matched by its text on scan page 666 (the OCR header on that run reads page 61; marked '?' by the corpus tool; the story cites scan page 666). The Bulletin 1923 entry (PDF p. 26) and the 1895 Lighthouse Board entry (scan p. 296) were confirmed by corpus.py page. 12. Name variants: 'Cale B. Stowe' (roster), 'Caleb Stowe' (nomination), 'Caleb B. Stowe' (1921 report), 'B. C. Stowe' (1919 paper). 'Clarence W. Salter' (roster), 'C. W. "Harry" Salter' (nomination), 'Clarence W. "Harry" Salter' (LighthouseFriends). 13. Roster: Thomas M. Davis (1861) overlaps Elizabeth Lusby's service to 1862 in the USLHS roster; no source read explains it. 14. Hours: the DNR page gives 'open daily from 8am to Sunset' and elsewhere 'open from sunrise to sunset'; the story states both. The TPLS page (copyright 2009-2022) says its season begins May 1 'this year' and gives no year; treated as provisional. The DNR walk distances (0.4 and 0.8 miles) are not used. 15. The nomination sentence beginning 'Because of this increased shipping, the Turkey Point Lighthouse' is cut off; not used. 16. Fannie Salter's age at appointment: 43 (LighthouseFriends) against 65 at retirement (nomination); not used. 17. The record's county 'Kent' is corrected to Cecil (see corrections). 18. Rebecca Crouch's death date reads 'July 1 1, 1895' in the OCR of the nomination; read as 11 July 1895 (the space is an OCR split).

corrections.why: The nomination gives 31 1/2 feet from the base to the parapet (9.6 m) and USLHS gives 30 feet to the lantern centre; 11.5 m (about 38 ft) matches neither.
The nomination places the light near North East, Cecil County, and the USLHS record lists Location County: Cecil.
The nomination describes a conical, brick tower; the timber and stone crib is its foundation (USLHS: Tower Foundation: Timber/Stone Crib).

resolved_conflicts.explanation: USLHS gives 1832 as the year the station was established; the nomination dates the tower to 1833 and LighthouseFriends says the light commenced operation in 1833. The story uses 1833 for the lit light and notes 1832.
Decommissioned April 2000 and leased in 2001; reactivated as a private aid to navigation on 30 November 2002 (LighthouseFriends, USLHS 'Private Aid: Yes'). Active now.
